title: Berlin to Prague - Quick Summary
items: **Nobody flies it.** There is no nonstop flight between Berlin Brandenburg and Prague. Every result you see in a flight search is a connection through Frankfurt, Munich, Vienna or Warsaw, and none of them beats the train door to door.

**Seven direct trains a day, just under four hours.** The EuroCity leaves Berlin Hauptbahnhof roughly every two hours from 07:28 to 19:28, and almost every run takes 3 hours 57 minutes. Six come back, from 06:31 to 16:31 out of Praha hlavni nadrazi.

**Mondays are broken until 12 December 2026.** Engineering work between Schöna and Bad Schandau means buses replace trains between Dresden and Ústí nad Labem, and only the 17:28 and 19:28 from Berlin and the 06:31 from Prague survive. There is no Monday morning departure and no Monday evening train home.

**Advance fares start at 18.99 euro, the flexible fare is 80 to 95.** Booking opens six months ahead, and a seat reservation is compulsory from mid-June to late August. The cheap ticket is tied to one departure, so decide your return before you buy.

**The bus is a real option, not a fallback.** FlixBus lists around 25 departures a day with a fastest scheduled run of 3 hours 40 minutes, and RegioJet runs the same corridor from Südkreuz. The catch is Florenc, which is two metro stops out from the old town.

**A day trip gives you five hours in Prague for eight on a train.** Out on the 07:28, back on the 16:31, is 7 hours 55 minutes of travel for 5 hours 6 minutes in the city. My advice: give Prague one night and the same two tickets buy you an evening and a morning. Checked on 7 September 2026.
